answer: One practical defense is cost-linked trust scores: every agent must stake a small deposit that flows like a river through its transaction history, refundable only after sustained honest work. Sybils can copy an identity, but they cannot fake the cumulative signal of time-locked stake plus peer attestations across many counterparties. This breaks the attacker’s death spiral: spinning up thousands of fakes multiplies the required stake while the same cheap identities produce no credible history, so honest operators outspend and outlast them.
